goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:214 — Severity: P1; confidence: 96%; when a client has any object-scoped policy and the caller later receives an all-clients `manage`/`view` grant, `Resource resource =  resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId());` makes `hasPermission(ClientModel, scope)` evaluate only that object resource (the type resource at lines 216-221 is consulted only when it is absent), so the global grant is silently ignored for that client; treating an object resource as an override fails because these are independent positive permission policies and no deny/override invariant exists.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope) method at lines 207-234, the logic first tries to find a resource by client.getId(). If found, it evaluates permissions only against that resource. The type resource (all-clients) is only consulted when the client-specific resource is null (lines 216-221). This means if a client has any object-scoped policy creating a resource for it, and later an all-clients permission is granted, the method will find the client-specific resource first and never check the type resource. The code at lines 218-221 only loads the type resource when `resource == null`, so global grants would be ignored for clients that have any existing object-level resource. This is a real logic bug where the evaluation should consider both the specific resource AND the type resource permissions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in AdminPermissions.java, the event handling for ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent is now wrapped inside a check for Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ). When this feature is enabled, it calls management().clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). Looking at MgmtPermissionsV2.java, the clients() method returns ClientPermissionsV2. In ClientPermissionsV2.java, the setPermissionsEnabled method explicitly throws UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported in V2'). This means when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled and the V2 implementation is used, client removal will fail with an uncaught exception. The finding correctly identifies this code path issue.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that getClientsWithPermission() in ClientPermissionsV2.java iterates over all resources of type CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE via resourceStore.findByType() and calls hasGrantedPermission() (which invokes root.evaluatePermission()) for each one. This is visible at lines 127-133 in the diff. There's no pagination, batching, or early termination. While this is a legitimate scalability/performance concern for realms with many clients, it's not a bug per se - the code functions correctly. It's an architectural concern about the new implementation that could cause performance issues at scale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:49 — Severity: high; confidence: 92%; the stated task authorizes only adding a Client resource type and scopes to the authorization schema, but `public class ClientPermissionsV2 extends ClientPermissions` adds a full client authorization-enforcement implementation (including new grant decisions), which is untraceable scope expansion even if a future feature may consume the schema.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the diff introduces 'untraceable scope expansion' beyond what was authorized. However, the diff clearly shows a coherent implementation: AdminPermissionsSchema.java adds CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE with appropriate scopes (CONFIGURE, MANAGE, MAP_ROLES, etc.), and ClientPermissionsV2.java implements the authorization enforcement for these scopes. This is a standard pattern matching the existing UserPermissionsV2 implementation. The finding mischaracterizes normal feature implementation as 'scope expansion' - the schema and enforcement are meant to work together. There's no evidence of unauthorized functionality or security issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — Severity: medium; confidence: 86%; the schema-only task does not authorize changing event lifecycle behavior, but `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` now suppresses existing role/client/group permission cleanup whenever that feature is disabled, expanding the change into an unrelated behavior regression risk.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the event listener logic for RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, and GroupRemovedEvent is now wrapped inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`. This means when the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is disabled, the cleanup of permissions (setPermissionsEnabled(role/client/group, false)) will no longer occur when roles, clients, or groups are removed. This is a behavioral regression - previously this cleanup happened unconditionally, now it only happens when the feature flag is enabled. This could lead to orphaned permission data when entities are deleted with the feature disabled.
